statusNote: The REGISTRY is implemented: registration, validation, lazy discovery and lifecycle are real, tested code. The skills themselves remain data, and nothing here executes a procedure. See notImplemented below.
definition: A Skill is procedural knowledge: rules, a procedure, a map of the capabilities the procedure would need, and validators that decide whether it may be selected. It is a document with a lifecycle, not an actor.
isNot: an agent — a skill has no goal, no loop and no autonomy
an Agent Machine — it does not schedule, delegate or supervise
a tool executor — it never invokes a tool, only names the capability an invoker would need
a permission grant — naming a capability is a requirement, never an authorisation
a runtime — nothing here executes anything
a model provider — a skill neither selects nor calls a model
authorityRule: A skill DECLARES requiredCapabilities. The capability system remains the sole authority on whether a caller may use them. Selection of a skill grants nothing: an invoker still has to pass capability negotiation, permission policy and approval on its own account. A skill that names `workspace.filesystem` has not been given the filesystem; it has stated that without the filesystem its procedure cannot be followed.

lifecycle.rule: Transitions are linear with an early exit to `released`. Nothing may skip a state: a skill cannot become `active` without having been `loaded`, because `active` asserts the body is in memory. No state implies execution authority — `active` means selected-and-loaded, not permitted-to-run.
lifecycle.noAuthorityRule: No transition grants, checks or carries permission. Reaching `active` is not an authorisation event, and the registry deliberately has no API that could make it one.

levels.L0: identity — id, title, one line. Always loaded; this is what `list` returns.
levels.L1: card — when to use it, what it needs, what it produces.
levels.L3: deep knowledge — references, examples, edge cases.

disclosure.rule: `list` and `resolve` read L0/L1 only. L2/L3 live behind a loader that is not called until `load`. Listing every skill's full body is how a context window is exhausted before any work begins, so lazy discovery is a contract requirement and not an optimisation.
disclosure.lazinessGuarantee: A registered skill's body loader must not be invoked by register, list, resolve, describe or validate-selection. Only `load` may invoke it.

operations.name: skill.list
operations.summary: Identities of every registered skill. Never loads a body.

operations.name: skill.resolve
operations.summary: One skill's identity by id, or null. Never loads a body.

operations.name: skill.describe
operations.summary: The card: when to use it, required capabilities, validators, degradation and replacement metadata. Still no body.

operations.name: skill.validate-selection
operations.summary: Answers whether this skill could be selected in a given context: are its required capabilities declared, is its contract compatible, do its validators pass. Returns a verdict; never throws for a normal negative answer.

permissionNote: Both permissions are read-shaped. There is deliberately no `ai:skill:execute`: execution is not a skill operation, so no permission may imply it. The namespace itself is subject to XA-8, which is open-for-manager.

trustLevels.core: Ships with the product. Its procedure was reviewed as part of the release.
trustLevels.untrusted: Provenance unknown or failed a check.

trustDegradation.rule: Trust never raises what a skill may require, it only lowers what it may be selected for. A `community` or `untrusted` skill that requires a destructive capability degrades to `requires-approval`; it is never silently selectable.
trustDegradation.defaultRationale: A skill whose trust is unstated is untrusted. Defaulting to `community` would let an omission buy privilege.

degradation.capability-unavailable: A required capability is not declared by any LEGO. The skill stays registered and listable, and is not selectable.
degradation.version-incompatible: The skill requires a contract major this registry does not implement.
degradation.optional-absent: An optional capability is missing; the skill is selectable and its card says which steps will not apply.
degradation.rule: Degradation is reported, never silently repaired. A skill is never auto-downgraded into a different procedure.

replacement.rule: A skill's procedure, knowledge and validators may be replaced entirely without consumers changing, provided id, contractVersion major and the card's declared inputs/outputs hold. `implementationVersion` moves freely; `contractVersion` follows semver and a major bump is a breaking change the gate detects.

compatibility.rule: A skill declares the skill-contract major it was written against. Same major = compatible. Different major = version-incompatible, refused at registration rather than at use, because a skill that cannot be selected should never appear selectable.

validators.rule: A validator answers a question about SELECTION. It may not perform I/O, call a tool, read a credential or touch the filesystem — it receives a plain context object and returns a verdict. Validators run during validate-selection, never during list or resolve.

mustNot: inherit authority from the Agent Machine
grant authority to the Agent Machine
touch the filesystem, terminal, git, browser, network or a model
security.failClosed: An unknown or undeclared required capability is refused. A skill referencing a capability no LEGO declares is registered-but-not-selectable, and validate-selection returns a negative verdict naming the capability. It is never assumed to be available.
security.grantsNothing: The registry exposes no API that returns a permission, a credential, a token or a handle. The strongest thing a caller obtains is a frozen description.

notImplemented: an interpreter or DSL for procedure steps
skill packs, distribution, signing or installation
an Agent Machine, or any binding to one
a model provider, tool gateway, MCP client or runtime adapter
memory, workspace or a context manager
persistence — the registry is in-memory and per-process by design

openDecisions.XA-11: Which contract publishes a skill, and is a skill a backend concept at all? Open-for-manager. This implementation deliberately does NOT settle it: `ai.skill` is declared under the existing ai-foundation domain rather than as a new top-level domain, so if the manager rules that skills are a frontend or shared concept, the contract moves without a domain having to be deleted.
openDecisions.XA-8: Which permission namespace do AI capabilities use? Open-for-manager. `ai:skill:*` follows the prevailing `ai:<concept>:<verb>` shape used by every other AI capability, so it moves with them if the manager renames the namespace.
